query.raw: To clarify, the letter grading means we will have GPA to apply to colleges, correct?  For our son, we're looking to enter TTK-12 for the upcoming school year, does that mean we should apply to the full time paid program closer to May 2027 and then get on the lottery system after that or is the 10/29 submission deadline in preparation for fall to begin 2027 school year, please?  Separately, our youngest will be entering 8th grade for the next school year starting August 2027; however, he previously skipped a grade.  We want to transfer him to a local online public school system that only begins in the 9th grade.  Would you know whether Texas will allow him to do 9th grade with TTK-12 and then repeat it in public school, so he doesn't enter public school system much younger than his in person peers for sports, please?

Grade Level Placement for Transfer Students

Students transferring to Texas Tech Middle School from an accredited public or private school will generally be placed at the grade level indicated by their previous school. An official transcript, report card or other required academic record must be provided to verify previous enrollment, completed coursework and grade-level placement.

Texas Tech K-12 courses are designed for students to begin at the start of a semester whenever possible. Students are encouraged to complete their current semester before withdrawing from their previous school.

Students who transfer before completing a semester may be required to complete additional coursework, intervention or placement assessments to determine appropriate course and grade-level placement.

Students transferring from a homeschool program or non-accredited school or program must provide available academic documentation, such as transcripts, grade reports or records of completed coursework. Texas Tech K-12 will review the student’s academic history and may require placement assessments or other academic evaluation to determine appropriate grade-level and course placement.

Texas Tech K-12 reserves the right to make the final determination regarding grade-level and course placement.

ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) USE POLICY

Artificial intelligence (AI) tools may be used to support student learning when their use is appropriate for the assignment or activity. AI should support, not replace, a student's own learning, critical thinking and communication.

Appropriate uses of AI may include brainstorming, clarifying concepts, creating study materials, generating practice questions or receiving feedback when permitted by the teacher or course.

Students may not use AI to generate graded work and submit that work as their own unless the teacher or course instructions specifically permit the use of AI for that assignment.

Students are responsible for the work they submit and must be able to independently explain and demonstrate their understanding of submitted work.

When the authenticity of submitted work cannot reasonably be verified, the teacher may require the student to participate in a discussion-based assessment or other method of verification. Verification may include a live, camera-enabled session.

Work determined to be inauthentic may be subject to resubmission requirements and academic consequences in accordance with Texas Tech K-12 policy.

answer.text:
**1. GPA and Letter Grades for College Applications**

- Yes, Texas Tech K-12 uses a letter and numerical grading system, and calculates an official GPA for all eligible coursework.
- This GPA is included on transcripts and can be used for college applications, including for universities that require a GPA for admission or automatic acceptance (such as UT Austin).

---

**2. Application Timing for Full-Time Paid Program vs. Tuition-Free Lottery**

- **Tuition-Free Program:**  
  - The next lottery deadline is **October 29, 2026** for students wishing to begin in the 2026–2027 school year.
  - If you want to be considered for the tuition-free program for Fall 2027, you should submit your application by the posted lottery deadline (October 29, 2026).
- **Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program:**  
  - Enrollment for the tuition-paid program is open year-round, as long as space is available.
  - You do **not** need to wait until May 2027; you can apply at any time for the tuition-paid program.
  - If you apply for the tuition-free program and are not selected, you are not automatically enrolled in the paid program—you must submit a separate application if you wish to enroll in the paid program.

---

**3. Skipping and Repeating 9th Grade for Your Youngest Child**

- Texas Tech K-12 allows students to enroll in 9th grade if they meet grade-level placement requirements.
- If your child completes 9th grade with Texas Tech K-12 and then transfers to a local public school, the receiving public school will review his transcript and determine grade placement.
- **Repeating 9th Grade:**  
  - Texas public schools generally review transcripts and may allow a student to repeat a grade, especially if requested for social or athletic reasons.
  - However, final placement decisions are made by the receiving school district, not Texas Tech K-12.
  - It is recommended to contact the local public school where you plan to enroll your child to confirm their policy on repeating 9th grade after completing it elsewhere, especially for athletic eligibility and age alignment with peers.

---

**Summary of Next Steps**
- Apply for the tuition-free program by October 29, 2026, for the 2027 school year, or apply to the tuition-paid program at any time.
- For your youngest, contact the intended public school district to confirm their policy on repeating 9th grade after attending Texas Tech K-12.
- For further assistance, contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.
